title: Finite type modules on a ringed space: stable under epimorphic images and extensions (Stacks 01B7)
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space (for instance a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with its structure sheaf) and $\mathit{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ the abelian category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules on the open sets of $X$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. An $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ is *of finite type* if every point $x\in X$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ and finitely many sections $s_1,\dots,s_n\in\mathcal F(U)$ such that the associated map $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F|_U$, $e_i\mapsto s_i$, is an epimorphism of $\mathcal O_U$-modules ([def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation] (1); on a scheme this is the notion of [pqf-def-coherent] (2)). Then: (1) if $p:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ is an epimorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules and $\mathcal F$ is of finite type, then $\mathcal G$ is of finite type (in particular the image $\operatorname{Im}\varphi=\operatorname{Ker}(\mathcal H\to\operatorname{Coker}\varphi)$ of a morphism $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal H$ whose source is of finite type is of finite type); (2) if $0\to\mathcal F_1\to\mathcal F_2\to\mathcal F_3\to0$ is a short exact sequence of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] and $\mathcal F_1$ and $\mathcal F_3$ are of finite type, then $\mathcal F_2$ is of finite type.

proof.text: For a finite family of quotient sections over U and a point x of U, use local lifting (1) to choose a lift of each section on an open neighborhood of x. Intersect these finitely many neighborhoods with U, and restrict the lifts to this common neighborhood. Naturality gives the simultaneous lifting equations. The extra intersection with U also handles an empty family.

proof.text: On a short exact complex whose outer objects have finite global generators, suppose the quotient generating map has a lift l to the middle object. Form the coproduct map from the free subobject generators and l. To prove this map epi, take a morphism t annihilating it. The subobject generators imply f composed with t is zero. Exactness and epi g descend t through g to d. The lifted quotient generators imply that their generating epimorphism composed with d is zero, hence d and t are zero. The epi cancellation criterion proves the coproduct map epi. Compose with freeSumIso inverse to obtain finite generators indexed by the sum of the two finite index types.

proof.text: At each x choose a generating open for each outer term, restrict the quotient generators to their intersection, and apply simultaneous local lifting. Restrict the subobject generators to the resulting neighborhood. Open restriction preserves the short exact complex. The previous coproduct argument supplies finite generators of the middle term there. The chosen neighborhoods, indexed by the points of X, cover X: intersect any test open W with the neighborhood of each x in W. This gives LocalGeneratorsData with finite generating families and proves the extension assertion, including the empty-space case.

split_report.summary: Split following Stacks 01B7 (modules.tex line 855) and its proof, read with Definition 01B5. Five elementary steps: (1) generation by finitely many sections tested on sections over a covering, from the existing same-unit lemma lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting (1) on (U,O_U); (2) clause (1): images of generators along an epimorphism generate ('trivial' in the source, written out with two refinements of coverings); (3) the image of a morphism with finite type source, via the cokernel and lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-iff-epi-kernel-lift, as the citers use it; (4)-(5) clause (2): sections of F_3 locally lift (local-lifting (1)), and the kernel of g is locally in the image of f (local-lifting (2)), so the generators of F_1 and the lifts of those of F_3 generate F_2 over a small open; the source's 'result for modules over a ring applied to stalks' is carried out on sections over coverings, which avoids stalks and any new node. Statement: kept, with the finite type notion now cited to def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation (1) (pqf-def-coherent is for schemes only) and the image made explicit as Ker(H -> Coker). No new nodes. Mathlib: SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType exists (definition only), recorded as mathlib_candidate; no lemma for images or extensions.
